subject.title: [Bug]: CLI relay exits silently with code 1 when session lane is blocked — no timeout or busy error surfaced

question: Should same-session CLI lane waits become a structured terminal busy result, and what exit/status contract should that result use?
rationale: The bug is real, but the durable fix changes caller-visible delivery semantics for blocked CLI dispatches, so code review alone should not choose the permanent contract.

options.title: Accept Structured CLI Busy Result
options.body: Land the linked PR or a replacement after preserving all source-CLI dispatch variants and documenting the chosen stderr, JSON, and exit-code behavior.

options.title: Keep Exit 1 With Stderr
options.body: Fix the silent failure by rendering a clear error while keeping the current generic exit status for compatibility-sensitive scripts.

options.title: Keep Queueing Semantics
options.body: Surface progress or timeout diagnostics without making lane wait a terminal busy rejection for normal CLI dispatches.

recommendation.title: Accept Structured CLI Busy Result
recommendation.body: Land the linked PR or a replacement after preserving all source-CLI dispatch variants and documenting the chosen stderr, JSON, and exit-code behavior.

likelyOwner.reason: The Gateway-backed CLI relay and current line ownership trace most clearly to steipete, and the decision is about that public CLI/Gateway contract.
